claims.text: Introducing tungsten or molybdenum into a high-entropy nanoalloy can improve its structural stability at high temperature.
Introducing tungsten or molybdenum into a high-entropy nanoalloy can improve its chemical stability at high temperature.
Tungsten and molybdenum are refractory-element candidates for this intervention.
Adding a refractory element can promote formation of a stable solid solution or homogeneous phase.
A refractory-element addition can reduce atomic diffusion rates in the alloy.
A refractory-element addition can increase the activation energy of degradation processes.
Reduced diffusion and increased degradation activation energy improve alloy stability.
The refractory-containing nanoalloy will be more structurally and chemically stable than an otherwise comparable nanoalloy without refractory elements.
Improved structural and chemical stability will enhance high-temperature performance and longevity.
The effectiveness of refractory-element addition depends on the alloy's specific composition.
The effectiveness of refractory-element addition depends on processing conditions.
The optimal refractory-element identity and addition level, and its interactions with other alloying elements, remain uncertain.
XRD and EDS can be used to examine phase structure and chemical homogeneity in refractory high-entropy materials.
Failure of the refractory-containing sample to outperform the refractory-free control in structural and chemical stability would falsify the hypothesis.
